decisions.detail: QUOTE: `MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(member)` renames each member for outside code... the default expansion is `private_##member`, so `ssl->MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(conf)` becomes `ssl->private_conf`. An application that touches `ssl->conf` directly therefore fails to compile instead of silently depending on the layout. | WHY: The answer says opacity is enforced at compile time by renaming members to `private_<name>`, so direct access fails to compile. It never says the struct layout stays visible, but the renaming mechanism is stated, and that is what the item requires. || QUOTE: `MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(member)` renames each member for outside code... the default expansion is `private_##member`, so `ssl->MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(conf)` becomes `ssl->private_conf`. The struct stays in the public headers.
